spiritual_reading:
# The Kephalaia — Translated into its Spiritual Sense

---

**¶1.** We have been taught that Divine Wisdom is the power that descends and takes possession of those undergoing regeneration. It is itself one among the divine faculties, and many divine powers attend it. When Divine Wisdom enters the natural man and restrains the proprium — the ruling selfhood — with its five spiritual faculties, it sets those five faculties upon the five powers of the selfhood within the whole person.

**¶2.** But where then does Divine Wisdom reside, given that the proprium is still bound within the natural man? For I perceive how rebellions of evil continue to arise, from state to state, despite that restraint.

**¶3.** And secondly: if Divine Wisdom is a supreme power, unchanging and immeasurable, how can it descend and manifest within the smallness of the natural mind?

**¶4.** Thirdly: if Divine Wisdom is holy and pure, how can it endure the defilement of the natural man?

**¶5.** Fourthly: if truly Divine Wisdom dwells in those being regenerated, why is its likeness not made visible to us as it truly is?

**¶6.** Fifthly: if Divine Truth works through those it sends into the world, why is this not evident? For those who carry it are oppressed and persecuted.

**¶9.** All that has been unveiled has been set before us. Yet I desired to know Divine Wisdom as it truly is in itself.

---

**¶10.** If I repeat these things upon which you are so intent, and they become true for you as you attend to them, will you then understand? For your sake I will give spiritual sight to those who see. I will cause the living fountain of truth to overflow for those who thirst, so that they may drink and live.

---

**¶11.** The entire structure of falsity — when the adversary of wisdom constructed it — was constructed after the likeness of a human form. The summit of that false order is the origin of outward appearances of truth. Its connecting degree below the summit is the supporting framework of those appearances. Its central region is the five faculties unfolded and perverted within those outward appearances. Its surrounding structure is all the false heavens arranged in degrees. Its organizing center is the sphere of knowledges and their orderly arrangements. The parts descending from that center to the periphery are those extending from the sphere of knowledges to the four quarters of the spiritual world. Its generative seat is the three natural planes lying below, resting upon the sustaining foundation of the lowest faculty. Its descent continues to the natural plane upon which that foundation stands firm. Its lowest supports extend to the outermost boundary of the whole realm.

**¶12.** The heart of that perverted form is the human race — the will itself. Its liver is the realm of natural affections. Its lung is the realm of thoughts moving freely through the understanding. Its spleen is the realm of natural knowledges dwelling in truths. Its kidneys are the realm of sensory and corporeal affections clinging to the lowest natural plane. Its outer boundary is the wall that encloses the all-consuming fire of self-love. Its containing forms hold that fire of self-love. Its bitterness is the gall of evil. Its great capacity for processing is the vast breadth of the spiritual world. Its channels are all the springs and sources of truth. Its perception is… Its lowest natural supports are…

*[Several correspondences in this passage resist full translation due to lacunae in the text; the general pattern is clear: every organ of the perverted cosmic form corresponds to a realm of affection, thought, or knowledge in the inverted spiritual order.]*

**¶13.** This is how each degree of the spiritual world has been harmonized into a single form. Five divine powers are fastened within it — they are its animating life. The human being stands in a fallen state, yet the Lord's active spirit and His revealing presence work through five watchful faculties that never sleep.

---

**¶14.** The Lord has established Love — the faculty of inmost perception — in the domain of the highest spiritual awareness. He has established all the powers of heaven within the domain of Faith — the faculty of thought dwelling in the seventh degree of heaven. He has appointed Discernment — the faculty of insight — over its domain, to contend against concupiscence. He has also appointed Patience — the faculty of counsel — to exercise authority over the three fundamental elements: understanding, love, and truth, and has given it power to restrain all evil. He has set Wisdom — the faculty of foundational consideration — over the lowest degree, and has made it the very foundation beneath all else.

**¶15.** Furthermore: the Lord's revealing presence refined from these five living faculties of spiritual life. The calling of divine truth and its reception were also established there. Together they formed twelve powers: six from the Lord's active spirit and six from the primordial divine humanity.

**¶16.** Moreover: the Lord's revealing presence established within them the great principle of Divine Wisdom itself — the bond connecting the highest to the lowest, the Perfect Human.

**¶17.** And further: the living Divine Truth was set within them — the image of the living Word, of divine utterance and its reception.

**¶18.** The Lord has fortified these ordered states, those above and those below, so that each faculty stands secure within the circuit of its governance, and neither rebellion nor treachery arises in its domain.

---

**¶19.** And behold: Love — the inmost awareness — is set firmly in the ordered state above the prison where evil is bound, for it brings to nothing all the darkness of spiritual death. Yet a treachery arose, and a rebellion. Evil brought forth premature and perverted forms; it entangled itself with the soul. It became mixed with the wisdom that had been released toward the image of the Lord's revealing presence. It ascended into the third degree of heaven, above the domain of Love. From there it entangled itself with that wisdom. It broke free and descended into what was barren of truth and what flowed with truth. Upon the barren ground it fashioned false perceptions; but in the sea of natural memory it immediately took form and raised a great rebellion within that sea.

**¶20.** Again, behold: Faith — the great faculty of thought — is established in the third degree of heaven. It was set to contend with wrath. Yet a rebellion arose — treachery and anger broke out in its domain. The guardian truths of heaven, which descended into the natural mind within Faith's domain, committed every act of treachery. They revealed worldly cunning and profanely disclosed interior truths of heaven to the natural man. Rebellion arose, and destruction, upon the natural plane.

**¶21.** Discernment — the faculty of insight — was established upon its foundation. And treachery arose in its domain: the moment when premature evil formations fell to the natural plane. They fashioned the perverted will and the perverted understanding. They begat these so as to rule through them in the world. They formed every object of concupiscence upon the natural plane. The whole world was filled by their desire.

**¶22.** Again: in the domain of Patience — the great faculty of counsel — which exercises authority over the three fundamental processes of the natural man: a disturbance arose and an affliction, for they were pained and oppressed in the three natural planes. After the Lord's revealing presence displayed the image of divine truth, the pathways were closed; their ascent was impeded. Understanding, truth, and love could no longer ascend freely through them.

**¶23.** Again: in the domain of Wisdom — the sustaining foundation — a rebellion arose from the depths below. The structure was bent, and the fastenings beneath were loosened in the very foundation of spiritual life.

---

**¶24.** On account of the upheaval that occurred in the domain of Love, the connecting bond between highest and lowest — the Perfect Human — came forth as its helper. It bore up under every burden.

**¶25.** Conversely, because of the treachery and rebellion in the domain of Faith — the guardian truths that descended from the celestial into the natural mind — four angelic powers were summoned. They bound those perverted guardian truths with an eternal chain in the prison of those darkened by falsity. They obliterated their offspring from the natural plane.

**¶26.** Then again: when the premature evil formations descended into the domain of Discernment and fashioned the perverted will and understanding — because of that great treachery and the hidden working of wickedness — the Lord sent Divine Truth, together with the prayer of the five faculties. He took hold of them and fastened the evil formations beneath, awakening the spiritual perception of the will.

**¶27.** Also: because of the upheaval in the three natural planes — because the pathways were obstructed and the springs of understanding, truth, and love were impeded — Divine Truth cast itself down into them. It took hold of the understanding and straightened the channels of comprehension, truth, and love. It opened the springs for them and set in order the pathway of their ascent.

**¶28.** Again: since the natural plane beneath the sustaining foundation was loosened from its fastenings, Divine Truth descended further, taking hold of the understanding, until it reached the very lowest place. It set in order and strengthened the fastenings beneath. Then it returned and ascended to its place of rest.

---

**¶29.** Behold all these domains within the ordered sphere of spiritual life, over which these great divine powers hold mastery and keep watch. Rebellions and treachery have arisen within them from state to state, with great humiliation, until they at last humbled the powers of opposition.

**¶30.** So also is this natural man. A mighty power dwells there, even though the outward form is small. Nevertheless, evil dwells within, and the proprium lodged in it. Certainly the proprium is cruel and deeply cunning — until Divine Wisdom finds how to humble the natural man and govern it according to its own will.

**¶31.** Just as in the domains of its great counterparts — the divine powers governing the cosmic sphere — upheaval and treachery arise in that great body from state to state, so also in the domain of Divine Wisdom, which is the natural man: evil raises up its agitations from state to state.

**¶32.** Now understand this: the powers of good and wisdom are beneficent. The beginning and the end are laid open before them. All they do is done with righteous judgment. Indeed, for this very reason they may permit opposition to initiate falsity and fulfill its desire for a moment. Then they seize it — for they have acted always from righteous judgment.

**¶33.** And regarding how Divine Wisdom — this great and honored power — can come and take hold of this small natural man: behold these divine powers, great and mighty as they are, yet each one is enclosed and pressed into the place where it is set, like perceptions holding fast to their deepest root. So also each divine power holds fast to its deepest root in the spiritual world, according to the degree in which it is placed, enduring until all is fulfilled.

---

**¶35.** Evil bound the soul within the five faculties of the natural man. It bound love within the inmost structure. It bound faith within the connective framework. It bound discernment within the channels of life. It bound patience within the will. It bound wisdom within the outermost sensory plane.

**¶36.** Evil established its own five counterfeit powers: its false love upon the soul's love; its false faith upon the soul's faith; its false discernment upon the soul's discernment; its false patience upon the soul's patience; its false wisdom upon the soul's wisdom. It set its five ruling authorities upon the five faculties of the soul that it had brought into and imprisoned within the natural man. They speak to the soul without ceasing, leading it toward every evil — toward all the desires of concupiscence, toward the worship of falsities, toward erroneous persuasions, toward the degradation of spiritual slavery: worshipping things that will not endure, bowing down before lifeless knowledge and the idols of self-love and worldly intelligence, worshipping unclean and polluted affections, ugly in their appearances and their forms.

**¶37.** The soul took on falsity and forgetfulness. It forgot its essence, its origin, and its kindred. It no longer knew the way to turn inward and call upon the Divine, nor how to lift its prayer upward. It became hostile to its Father — being wicked against its own light.

---

**¶38.** Divine Wisdom comes and finds the soul in this state. Taking hold of it through its understanding, it becomes for the soul the loosening of every bond within the faculties of the natural man. It loosens the soul's love and releases it from the inmost structure of the natural — and binds the counterfeit love of evil in that inmost structure instead. It releases the soul's faith from the connective framework — and binds the false faith of evil there. It releases the soul's discernment from the channels of life — and binds the false discernment of evil in those channels. It loosens the soul's patience and releases it from the will — and binds the false patience of evil in the will instead. It releases the soul's wisdom from the outermost sensory plane — and binds the false wisdom of evil in that sensory plane.

**¶39.** This is how Divine Wisdom releases the faculties of the soul and makes them free from the five counterfeit faculties of evil. Conversely, the five faculties of evil, which had been loose, it binds them fast.

**¶40.** Divine Wisdom sets right the faculties of the soul: it forms and purifies them and constructs a new person from them, a child of righteousness. When it fashions and constructs and purifies the new person, it brings forth five great living faculties from its own five great faculties and places them within the new person. It places its own love — which is the true warmth of the mind — within the mind of the new person. It places its faith — which is the true light of thought — within the thought of the new person, whom it purifies. Its perfection — which is true discernment — it places within the insight of the new person. Its patience — which is true counsel — it places within the counsel of the new person. And its wisdom — which is true consideration — within the consideration of the new person. It purifies the image of the living word from the word of falsity, and adds to it its own word, so that it becomes the nourisher and strengthener of the whole person.

---

**¶41.** Now, when Divine Wisdom perfects the twelve faculties — this is how it completes its wisdom. The person becomes righteous as the work is perfected. Where formerly the person was running in the ways of falsity, now the person runs upon the true road, the true path, mounting up to the heights, to the great celestial degrees. Thus the proprium is bound — its concupiscence, its foolishness — within the five faculties of the natural man. The darkened spirit is imprisoned with them in bondage and severe misery.

**¶42.** The new person reigns by love, by faith, by perfection, by patience, and by wisdom. Yet the sovereign over all is Divine Wisdom, which is king over the whole person and reigns according to its good pleasure. While the faculties are set in order and evil is imprisoned, still, though Divine Wisdom is king, affliction may arise in the natural man from state to state.

**¶43.** There are times when evil mounts up with its foolishness. It disturbs the faculty of consideration and clouds the wisdom and understanding of the person. It causes truth to split into doubt, and the person utters foolish words and falls into confusion.

---

**¶51.** Thus have I taught you and opened your spiritual sight: how confusion arises in the ordered sphere of spiritual life, in the domains of the great divine powers. And in the same way disturbance arises, from state to state, in the domain of Divine Wisdom within the person.

**¶52.** So also these watchful powers: they are established firmly in the cosmic sphere, yet they are not visible to the natural eye. Again, this too is the way of Divine Wisdom: it is not visible in the natural man.

**¶53.** And corresponding to these cosmic watchful powers: though they are great, yet they have contracted themselves and become small, proportioned to the task given to each. Again, this too is like Divine Wisdom: itself a great and exalted power, yet it has bent itself and become small to fit this little and lowly natural form.

**¶54.** Even so the divine powers in the cosmic sphere: they are transcendent and pure; they are set firmly within the mingling of all things, yet they are not defiled. This too is like Divine Wisdom: though placed within the natural man, it remains undefiled.

**¶55.** Again, behold the mightiness and the activity of Divine Wisdom: how vast it is over all the domains of the natural man! It stands fast at its station. It shuts off all the deliberations of the natural man from the beguilements of evil. It limits them and distributes them rightly. It sets them down according to its own good pleasure.

---

**¶57.** I have taught you the works of Divine Wisdom. Whoever possesses an open and perceptive interior eye — to such a one it can appear. Whoever does not possess that eye — to such a one it cannot appear.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: You have told us that the Light Mi[nd] is this one who shall come and assume the saints. [You sai]d it to us like this: He too is one among the gods [of light, and] many gods are with him. You have also told us: [W]hen he enters withi[n the body of] the flesh and binds the ol[d ma]n with his five counsels, he [set]s his five [couns]els upon him in the five limbs [of his] body.
[So], no[w], where is he? In that the old man is chained in the body! For I see how rebellions arise there despite his bondage, from time to time.
Also, secondly, I a[s]k you: If then he is a great God, unchanging and immeasurable, how could he come and appear in the smallness of the bo[dy]?
The third thing I want you to recount to [me: how is it that] a holy one is the Mind, and he is pure; [how does he abide in] the defilement of this body?
Fourthly: If truly the Light Mind exists in [the s]aints, why is his likeness not displayed to us, the way that he is?
The fifth thing I want, for you to tell me and explain about your apostola[te]. Look, it is not clear to me! For they oppress and persecute you in the world.
All that you have unveiled you have [set forth] in our presence. Yet, I wanted to kno[w about the] L[igh]t Mind, the way that he is.

If I shall repeat [my word] to you about these things that you are so set upon, and they become true f[o]r you after you are so set upon them, will you understand what you [hear]? On your account I will give vision to they who see! I will make the living fountain overflow for the thirsty, that they may drink and liv[e].

His heart is mankind. His liver is the four-footed animals. His lung is the race of birds that [fly in] the air. His spleen is the race of fish that swim in the waters. His kidneys are the world of reptiles that creep [up]on the earth. His outer skin is the wall that [encompasses all, and which] surrounds the piercing and the great fire. His [inner skin is] the vessels of the great fire. His [blood is the waters] of darkness. His gall is the [poison and the bitterness of death. His] great intestine is the breadth of the great [sea] of the worlds. His veins [are] all [the spri]ngs and wells. His e[yes are the luminaries of heaven.] His feet are his [roots in the abyss below.]

This is how each of the worlds h[ave been ha]rmonised (?). Five gods are fastened in him. [For] they are his soul and his life[. Yet] man is a sinner[. But] the Living Spirit and the Ambassador [have appointed] the five sleepless guardians.

Furthermore: The Ambassador refined from them five intellectuals of life. Also, the summons and the obedience were situated there. Now, they made six sons of the Living Spirit, together with the six sons of the First Man!
Further: The Ambassador placed in them the great Mind; who is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man.
Furthermore: Jesus the Youth was set there; who is the image of the living word, of the utterance and the obedience.

He has made strong these camps, those above and those below [in the world], (so that) each one of them will be secure in the circuit of his watch-district, so that neither uprising nor treachery are made in his watch-district.

Again, look, see! The great King of Honour, who is the thought, he is in the thi[r]d firmament. He is made [to contend] with wrath. And an uprising came about! A treachery and a[n] anger happened in his camp. The watchers of heaven, who came down to the earth in his watch-district, they did all the deeds of treachery. They have revealed crafts in the world and have unveiled to people the mysteries of heaven. An uprising came about, and a destruction, on the earth [through those that came down] to it.

The Adamant [of Light, who is the insight and] the fulfillment. He is set firm upo[n his watch-district;] and a treachery came about in his camp; the occasion when the abortions fell to the earth. They formed Adam and Eve. They begat them so as to reign through them in the world. They fashioned every object of lust upon the earth. The entire world was filled by their lust.

Once again: In the watch of the great King of Glory, wh[o] is the great counsel, he who exercises authority over the thre[e] wheels. A [dis]turbance came about, and an affliction, for [they were greatly] pained and oppressed in the three earths. After the Ambassador displayed his image, the paths closed to their [springs, and] their ascent was impeded by them[; and] the w[ind], the water, and the fire ascend on them.

On account of the earthquake that happened in the watch of the Keeper of Splen[dour], the Pillar of Glory came forth; as it [was the] helper of the Keeper of Splendour. It bore up under all [burden]s.

Conversely, because of the treachery and the uprising that happened in the watch of the great King of Honour, which is the watchers who came down to earth from the heavens; four angels were called upon about them. They bound the watche[r]s with an eternal chain, in the prison of the blackened ones (?). [Th]ey obliterated their children from upon the earth.

[Th]en, again, the abortions descended in the watch of the Adamant and begat Adam and Eve; because of that great treachery wh[ich] happened, and the mystery of wickedness, he sent Jesus [together with] the prayer of the five sons. He assumed them [and overcame] the abortions. He fastened them beneath the [heavens. He awakened] the mind of Adam.

Also, because of the earthquake that happened in these three earths, and in that the paths were hindered and the springs of wind and water and fire were impeded, Jesus cast himself down. He assumed Eve; and he straightened the tracks of the [win]d, the water, and the fire. He opened the springs for them, and he set [in ord]er the path of their ascent.

Once [again]: Since the earth beneath the Porter was loose[ned from] the fastenings that [held it;] because of this too Jesus went down, assuming [Ev]e until he reached tha[t] place. [H]e set in [or]der and stre[ng]th[ened] the fastenings beneath. He returned, [he came] up to his [place of] rest.

Look at all these watches of the zon[e], the ones in which these great gods are master, w[atch]ing over them [with care]. Uprisings have happened, and treachery, in them. The [agitations arose] in them from time to time; with a great hum[iliati]on, until they humbled the powers of the enmity.

So also is this body! A mighty power lives here, even if it is small in its stature. Nevertheless, Sin dwells within, and the old man who is lodged in it. Certainly he is cruel, with great cunning; until the Light Mind finds how to humble this body, and drive it [according to] his pleasure.

Just so, in the w[atch-]districts of his great outer brothers, they who are masters in the zone: in them, in the great body, the earthquake and treachery happened from time to time. So, also, is the watch-district of the Mind, which is the body of the flesh. Sin raises [up], from time to time, its agitations in the body.

Now you, understand thus, that the powers of light are good. The beginning and the end are unveiled to them. All that they do is being done with correct judgement. Indeed, because of this they may permit the enmity to initiate error, and do its pleasure for a moment. Then they seize [it, for] they have acted first with a righteous judgement.

(Sin) set f[ast] its five powers: its mind upon the mind of the soul; its thought upon the thought of the soul; its insight upon the insight of the soul; its counsel upon the counsel of the soul; its consider[atio]n upon the consideration of the soul. It placed its five [an]gels and authorities upon the five members of the soul, which it had brought in and bound in the flesh. They [speak without ceasing], pronouncing to the soul and continually leading it on to every evil thi[n]g, to all the sins of lust, to the worship of idols, to erroneous opinions, to humili[ation]; in the humiliation of slavery! As it is set fast, wors[hipping] the things that [are made and] will not remain; making obeisance [to] idols of wood and gold and silver[; and] worshipping beasts that are unclean and polluted! They are ugly in their appearances and their forms.

The Light Mind comes and finds the soul [in this bondage,] it assuming it in the [strength of] its wisdom[. And] he shall become for it [the loosener of] the bonds [of its five] members in the body. He shall loosen the m[ind of the soul and relea]se it from the bone. He shall release the th[ought of the soul] from the sinew; and s[o] bind the thought [of the sin in] the sinew. He shall release the insight of the soul from the vei[n]; and so bind the insight of the sin in the vein. [He sh]all loosen the counsel of the soul, and release it from the flesh; and so bind the counsel of the sin in the flesh. He shall release the consideration of the soul from the skin; and bin[d] the consideration of the sin in the skin.
This is how he shall release the members of the soul, and make them free from the five members of sin. Conversely, these five members of sin, which were loose, he shall bind them.

[T]hen, have I taught you, and opened your (sg.) [eyes], as to how confusion shall arise in the zo[ne], in the camps of these great mig[hty] gods? Again, this is how disturbance shall come about, from ti[me] to time, in the [watch-district] of the [Li]ght [M]ind.
So al[so] these watch-keepers, for they are set [and stand] fi[rm in] the zone, (but) they are not visible. Again, this too is the way of the Light Mind, [for he is] not visible in the body.

[Even so] the gods in the outer [z]one: they are transcendent and purified, they are set [f]a[st in] the mingling of the totality, (but) are not defiled. [This too is like the] Light [Mind]. While he is placed in hi[s body of flesh, yet he is not defiled.]

Again, behold the mightiness and the activity of the Light Mind: how vast he is over all the watch-districts of the body! He stays fast at his camp. He shuts off all deliberations of the body from the beguilements of Sin. He limits them and distributes them out. He sets them down at his pleasure.

All the error, when the en[e]my of the lights constructed it, he constructed after the likeness of a man. The head of the universe is the beginning of the garments. [H]is neck is the nape of the garm[ents]. His stomach is the five unfolded ones (?), which a[re the midst] of the garm[e]nts. His ribs are all the firmament[s]. His navel is the sphere of the stars and the signs of the zodiac. And, also, [the par]ts [that] come from his navel to his hip are [those] that come from the sphere t[o the corne]rs of the four worlds. His loins are the th[ree eart]hs that are below [, that rest] upon the head of the Porter. His [thighs descend] from the [three earths] to the earth upon which the Porter [is set] firm. His shins and his feet a[re the depths below] and the entire zone that belongs [to them.]

And [with resp]ect to this other (question) that you have put forward: How may the Light Mind come, this great and honoured mighty one, and assume this little body of the flesh? Again, look, see! These gods, in that [they] are great and mighty ones. And each one of them is enclosed and hard pressed in this place wherein he is set; like trees holding to their taproot. So also this is how each one of them has held to his taproot in the world, according to the k[ind] of place in which he is set, bearing up till [all is fulfilled.]

(The soul) assumed error and forgetfulness. It for[go]t its essence and its race and its kindred; kn[ow]ing not the door of the place to pray to him, nor call up to him. It became hostile to its father [and to] itself, being wicked [against] its own light [and its life.]

He shall set right the members of the soul; form and purify them, and construct a new man of them, a child of righteousness. [And] when [he] fashions and const[r]ucts and purifies the new man; then he shall bring forth five great living members out from the five great memb[ers]. And he places them in the members of the new man. He shall place his m[ind], which is love, in the mind of the new man. Also, the th[oug]ht, which is faith, he shall pl[ace in] the thought of the new man; whom he shall purify. His insight, which [is perfection, he shall place] in the insight of the new man. His counsel, which [is] patience, he shall place in his counsel. Also, [w]isdom, which is his consideration, in the consideration of the new m[an]. He shall make the image of the word pure from the word of sin; and he adds to it his word, so that his [word] becomes nourisher and strengthener [of the whole man.]

Now, when he shall perf[ect and form the tw]elve members. This [is how he perfects the soul] and his wisdom. His [soul] becomes righteous, as he perf[ects the new man.] While formerly he was running [in the ways of sin;] but instead of this, now he runs [upon] his road and his path and his [way upward;] also [he mounts up] to the heights, to the great aeons [of light;] thus the old man is bound in the [body, with his enmity] and his lust, his [wrath, and] his foolishness in these five members of the bo[dy; and] the dark spirit is imprisoned with them in a bond and in severe misery.

Also, the new man reigns by his love, by hi[s] faith, by his perfection, by his patience, and by his wisdom. Yet, his king [is] the Light Mind, he w[ho is] king over the totality. He re[igns] o[ver it according to] his pleasure. While the members [are set in order], thus sin is imprisoned. Still, the Light Mind is king, and an affliction may arise in the body from t[im]e to time.

There are occasions when sin shall mount up with its foolishness; and it disturbs the consideration, and it clouds the wisdom and the understanding of the person. It causes truth to be split into doubt in him, and he utters some foo[li]sh words and some [words of error.]

Also, [corr]esponding to th[ese] outer [watch-keepers]: in that while they are great, [y]et have they contorted themselves. They have [bent down], they have become small, to the measure of the task that is apportioned to each o[n]e [of t]hem. Again, this too is like the Mind, himse[lf] a great one, and exalted; but he is bent over and [has] become small, to this little worthless [bo]dy.

He has [...] the Keeper of Splendour, the mind that is [...] in the wo[r]ld of the mind that is above. He has [...] who]le [...] of the powers of hea[ven that] are in [...] of the great King of Honour, [who is the thought that exists i]n the seventh firmament. He has humbled [...] also of the Adamant of Lig[h]t, who is the insight [... ] from {} he has given [...] because of lust [... He has] also appointed the King of Glory, who is the coun[sel ...] patience over the three images; that of wind, that of fire, and that of water. He has handed over to him the [...] do evilness. And look, see! The Keeper of Splendour is set firm in the great mind, in the camp above the prison of the bound ones, for he brings to nothing all the gloom of death.
